findings.detail: resource_map keys resources by (type, slug, archived) and collapses a canonical/legacy duplicate to one via _preferred_resource, but metadata_index builds one entry per covered file and plan_derivations returns one record per entry. Reproduced at head in an isolated project with docs/plans/foo.html and docs/foo.html both declaring slug foo with 3 implementable sections: the resource_map path returns (3, 0) counting 1 plan, the index path returns (6, 0). Not hit on the real repository (parity holds at [111, 77]) and not covered by the new test fixture, so the done-when's parity claim is narrower than its wording. Double-counting inflates the remainder, which is the fail-safe direction for a closure decision, so it is a correctness gap rather than a hazard.
findings.evidence: review-measure-arms.log; run dir dup.py experiment (docs/plans/foo.html + docs/foo.html -> resource_map (3,0) vs index (6,0))
findings.title: the index path counts a duplicate-slug plan twice where the resource walk counts it once

item_verdicts.diff: read revision by revision against base 71b487a2b76e1654e3a40b38c784031972783663: 99df7dd0 changes reckon/crew/runs.py and reckon/metadata_index.py and adds tests/test_drain_reads_the_index.py, d4f75378 hardens the unreadable-plan path in the same two source files, and ae00894c adds the evidence fragment; nothing else moves.
item_verdicts.done_when: §4 item 1's done-when is parity of the cached derivation with the uncached one plus the sub-0.5 s fresh-process target; I reproduced the parity ([111, 77] both arms on the real repository) and the target (0.07-0.48 s index-current vs 6.3 s base), with the duplicate-slug caveat in findings.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, the three revisions, the gate command with 344/349 passed EXIT=0, a negative_control_log path, measurement_module/measurement_cwd for the scratch base arm, and baseline_suite/after_suite as the two gate arms.
item_verdicts.write_paths: git diff --name-only lists exactly reckon/crew/runs.py, reckon/metadata_index.py, tests/test_drain_reads_the_index.py and docs/evidence/fragments/the-obligations-hook-reads-a-snapshot/drain-reads-the-index.html, all within the declared scope, with no plan meta edit.

justifications.durability: tests/test_drain_reads_the_index.py pins the behaviour the change claims: a parity case against a read-every-plan recomputation with a positive control that the answer is non-trivial, a call-count control proving a second unchanged call parses no plan, a one-changed-plan case proving only the moved file is parsed again, an archived-plan case keeping the walk's exclusion, and an unreadable-plan case proving the inventory goes unknown and is rebuilt rather than answered from a figures-less row. The instrument is a read_state call counter, itself controlled by an assertion that the first call parsed every plan and the archived one. The one gap is that no test exercises a duplicate slug across a canonical and a legacy path, which is where I found the parity divergence.
justifications.evidence: The reviewed run's two arms are both green and carry no failing id: gate-base.log revision 71b487a2 344 passed EXIT=0 and gate-head.log revision d4f75378 349 passed EXIT=0 (the +5 are this node's new test file), so added_failure_count is 0. I reproduced the head gate file independently (tests/test_drain_reads_the_index.py 5 passed EXIT=0) and the declared negative control (RECKON_TEST_DRAIN_REREADS_EVERY_PLAN=1 -> 4 failed, 1 passed, EXIT=1, the four cost/parity cases the mutation should redden). I reproduced parity on the real repository myself: base [111, 77] at 6.30 s and head [111, 77] with the index current, so the index backs the same answer the full read gives. Deduction rather than a full mark: the done-when's parity is proven on a fleet whose plans have unique slugs, and I found the two implementations diverge when a project carries the same slug at a canonical and a legacy path (see findings).
justifications.fit: The change follows the module's own idioms: a plan record stored beside the served fields so ROW_FIELDS and /_index are unchanged, a schema-version bump rather than a defensive absence check, and a _row_is_complete predicate so a plan row written without its record is rebuilt on the next call. _plan_record deliberately reads the file itself rather than the memoised text parse_meta shares, because that memo reports an unreadable file as an empty document, and its docstring says so. The fit gap is that plan_derivations inherits the index's per-file row model, which does not deduplicate the way resource_map does, so the drain's semantics shift for a duplicate-slug tree.
justifications.goal_fidelity: §4 item 1 asks runs._project_executable_remainder to answer from the persisted metadata index instead of calling read_state on every plan, with each row revalidated by one stat and the rows gaining each plan's open-followup and implementable-section counts. That is exactly what landed: reckon/crew/runs.py replaces the resource_map+read_state loop with metadata_index.plan_derivations, reckon/metadata_index.py adds the plan record (_plan_record derives open_followups as the count of non-resolved followups and implementable_sections via plan_executable_remainder) and plan_derivations re-stats every covered file on each call, and the entry schema version moves 1->2 so a pre-change index is rebuilt. The plan's target is under 0.5 s in a fresh process; I measured the index-current arm at 0.07-0.48 s over six fresh processes on the real repository against a base arm of 6.30/6.34 s.
justifications.scope_discipline: The three revisions touch exactly reckon/crew/runs.py, reckon/metadata_index.py, tests/test_drain_reads_the_index.py and the one evidence fragment; git diff --name-only across 71b487a2..ae00894c lists only those four paths, all inside the node's declared write paths, and no plan meta line or shared index is edited. Each message carries a conventional subject and a body, and no plan, sprint or ticket identifier and no attribution trailer appears in the messages.
